pdfs.label: RP
pdfs.pageNumberConvention: 1-based PDF page; viewed pages show the same printed number

observations.literalObservationParaphrase: The compulsory Fundamentum uses carboxylic alkyl esters as ester-synthesis examples. The compulsory Leistungskurs Additum prescribes nucleophilic substitution via an addition-elimination mechanism and acid/alkaline hydrolysis. The separately shaded enrichment/networking box names amides, acid anhydrides and acid chlorides as further possible derivatives and names the influence of carbonyl activity on reaction rate and equilibrium.
observations.courseBoundary: The named acid derivatives and carbonyl-activity topic are in the grey enrichment box, not compulsory Additum. The quoted LK table label belongs to the mechanism column, not automatically to every grey enrichment item.
observations.wholeGoalLimit: There is no displayed comparative three-class acyl-substitution sequence or comparative leaving-group model/data on the viewed complete page. This observation alone is not a theorem that author operationalization is impossible.

observations.literalObservationParaphrase: The framework allows didactic/methodical freedom. Enrichment/networking examples are neither exhaustive nor exclusive. Optional selected blocks are taught with enough breadth/depth for their essential competency-oriented content.
observations.wholeGoalLimit: An open enrichment/example list allows authored teaching choices; it does not itself bind the whole current comparative goal to official source evidence.

observations.literalObservationParaphrase: Fundamentum applies to Grundfach and Leistungsfach; Additum applies to Leistungsfach. Scope and depth differ, and colored hour labels distinguish compulsory and optional blocks.

The illustrated layout distinguishes an optional LK Additum from a compulsory Fundamentum and distinguishes optional/compulsory course assignments. These examples explain the table grammar; page21 is not the real 3.3 ester source page.

S11-S14 cover arrangement/property explanation, transformation/bond changes, binding/interaction models and selected reaction mechanisms. This names general operations, without the current derivative-comparison operands.

E4 includes variable control in model/experimental procedures; E7 selects models; E8 identifies data relationships and explains them through theory; E9 discusses model limits. These general operators do not provide a missing derivative or lactone comparison model.

K10 requires coherent chemical argument; B3 considers the adequacy and limits of data. These operators are useful for operationalizing an established subject model and cannot supply absent subject scope.

pdfs.label: HE
pdfs.pageNumberConvention: 1-based PDF page; viewed pages show the same printed number

observations.literalObservationParaphrase: Q1.3 basic course content includes hydroxy/amino-acid structural constitution and carboxylic ester nomenclature, ester group, structural/skeletal formulas, condensation/ester formation and mechanistic consideration of ester synthesis. Acid and alkaline ester hydrolysis are also listed.

The Q1.3 elevated addition is mechanistic alkaline ester hydrolysis and di-/tricarboxylic-acid structure. Q1.5 elevated content separately covers structural properties and quantitative determination of ascorbic acid and paraben use.
observations.wholeGoalLimit: These complete topic pages do not display a lactone ring-closure model with formation/stability comparison. The ascorbic-acid structural context is a different source topic and is not a substitute for the current whole lactone goal.

pdfs.label: ST
pdfs.pageNumberConvention: 1-based PDF page; viewed pages show the same printed number

observations.literalObservationParaphrase: The eAN practical focus covers controlled reaction conditions, experiments, data recording/evaluation and chemical-source reasoning. It is a neighboring practical focus, not the organic ester content cell.

The organic eAN focus systematizes substitution/addition/elimination, extends selected reaction types to mechanisms including ester SN, explains structure/property relations for alkanals, alkanoic acids, esters and benzene, and names ester synthesis as an addition-elimination mechanism.
observations.wholeGoalLimit: The complete table restricts its displayed structure/property list and mechanisms to these selected contexts. It does not establish the current three-derivative comparison or condition-dependent lactone formation/stability comparison. This eAN route is not inferred from Hessen LK or the broad current jurisdiction list.

officialHTMLResponses.name: BY-C11-NTG
officialHTMLResponses.observationParaphrase: C11 is explicitly NTG. It applies condensation mechanisms to carboxylic esters/amides and derives reactants/reaction type from selected drug structures. The explanatory content limits the mechanism to ester/amide formation in simple drug retrosynthesis. This does not prescribe the current three-class reactivity comparison or whole lactone comparison.
